'''David Gilbert Luenberger''' (September 16, 1937 – May 19, 2026)<ref>{{cite book |title=IEEE Membership Directory, Volumes 1–2 |year=2001 |page=275 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LhdTAAAAMAAJ&q=david+luenberger+1937 }}</ref> was an American mathematical scientist known for his research and his textbooks, which center on [[mathematical optimization]]. He was a professor in the department of Management Science and Engineering at [[Stanford University]].

== Biography ==
Luenberger was one of the original founders of the Department of Engineering-Economic Systems in 1967. He served as chairman of the department for eleven years. He worked as a professor at the University for 50 years, retiring as of September 2013.

He has over 70 technical publications on [[Dynamic system|systems]] and [[optimal control|control]], in [[Optimization (mathematics)|optimization]], in [[microeconomics]], and in [[financial engineering]].<ref>[https://www.stanford.edu/dept/MSandE/people/faculty/luenberger/ MS&E | People | Faculty | Luenberger<!-- Bot generated title -->]</ref> His ''Investment Science'' is widely prescribed and referenced by finance academics and practitioners.

He received his [[B.S.]] in [[Electrical Engineering]] from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1959, and he received his [[Ph.D.]] in Electrical Engineering from [[Stanford University]] in 1963. His PhD thesis was titled, "Determining the State of a Linear System with Observers of Low Dynamic Order".<ref name=PhD-thesis>{{cite thesis|accessdate=March 15, 2025
|url=https://www.proquest.com/openview/fe250e7d710f8a87f66113ff03577ae3/1?cbl=18750&diss=y&pq-origsite=gscholar
|title=Determining the State of a Linear System with Observers of Low Dynamic Order
|degree=Ph.D.|department=Electrical Engineering|location=Stanford University|year=1963}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=David Luenberger|url=https://profiles.stanford.edu/david-luenberger|publisher=profiles.stanford.edu|accessdate=14 August 2015}}</ref> In his dissertation Luenberger introduced new methods for construction of [[state observer]]s. The celebrated [[Luenberger observer]] is named after him.

Luenberger died on May 19, 2026, at the age of 88.<ref>{{Cite web |title=David G. Luenberger, pioneer in optimization theory, dies at 88 |url=https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2026/07/david-g-luenberger-longtime-stanford-engineering-professor-who-brought-mathematical-rigor |access-date=2026-08-04 |website=news.stanford.edu |language=en}}</ref>
